column1: # RECURSIVE SCHEMAS (docs/design/RECURSION.0.md): where RefVal's
# prefix test used to answer path_cycle, it answers a RECURSIVE
# RESIDUAL -- `$.Node` inside `Node` (and `%t` inside `%t`) simply
# means the fixpoint. The residual expands ONE LEVEL PER MEET WITH
# CONCRETE STRUCTURE (per destination, ADR-005's clone discipline), is
# SYMBOLIC in canon and the aon1- hash (the mu-form, finite and
# round-tripping), and REFUSES at generation when a demanded position
# never met data (recursion_unexpanded) -- so guardedness is EMERGENT:
# `next?:` drops, `*null | $.Node` generates, a required recursive
# field with no data refuses at the instance. Termination is
# structural descent on finite data, with the depth budget as backstop
# (recursion_budget). VALUE cycles (mutual `a:$.b b:$.a`, chains,
# func-routed) are the chase detector's and still refuse path_cycle.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).

column1: # The expansion path is the INSTANCE's, wherever the residual came
# from. A residual carried inside a copied definition body (chain:
# $.spec.S inside P, copied to a slot shallower than the definition)
# inherited the copy's rebase-overlay tail in the TypeScript port,
# and the deep finding read $.p.chain.S.then.v there while Go said
# $.p.chain.then.v. The expansion clone now rebases to the DRIVE
# path unless the residual was lifted out of its defining tree (the
# vet --at row below), where the stored schema-namespace path is the
# one every anchored finding uses.
expansion-path-through-copied-body

column1: # vet --at over a recursive schema: the anchored meet lifts the

# (AontuContext._fixroot / Ctx.fixroot): depth-1 data is checked, and
# the finding sits in the schema's own namespace, as every anchored
# finding does. Before, the residual held its peer forever and bad
# data at depth vetted VALID unchecked.
